These probabilities come from my own reasoning about the cell structure and typical NAS-Bench-201 behaviour. I did not look anything up or run any code. The main patterns I relied on:

- **Replacing a strong op:** an edit that swaps out a strong op (claims 2 and 29) gives a lower effect than the same edit applied to other starting ops.
- **Filling an empty edge:** an edit that fills an edge currently set to `none` (claims 8 and 16) gives a higher effect.
- **Dead path:** an edit on a path that is already dead because of the parent (claim 22) gives a lower effect.
- **Other claims:** the rest are weak interactions, so I kept them in the low-to-middling range.
